vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-127041 - Using encrypted credentials in Bizum Pay for Android
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-127041
  
Published : Nov. 26, 2026, 10:02 a.m. | 19 minutes ago
  
Description :Bizum Pay for Android incorporates static values within the APK to authenticate and sign requests to its API, including those for user registration. These values are common across different installations and can be extracted from the APK. An attacker who obtains the application could reuse them to generate requests that the server accepts as authenticated. The potential scope of these requests was limited to querying auxiliary information and certain configuration statuses. Under no circumstances could they generate unauthorised payments via Bizum Pay, nor could they carry out illegitimate activations of the app (which always require access to the customer’s banking channels, thereby protecting them from this type of potential vulnerability). Furthermore, requests are always limited to a set number of attempts and are closely monitored to prevent potential mass queries.



The correction implemented uses site-specific material and removes support for the previous format in the backend. Consequently, previous versions are no longer operational for the services affected.
  
Severity: 8.8 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-131687 - ShopMagic <= 4.9.5 - Unauthenticated Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature to Guest Impersonation and Arbitrary Guest Profile Modification via 'shopmagic_visitor_' Cookie
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-131687
  
Published : Nov. 26, 2026, 9:33 a.m. | 48 minutes ago
  
Description :The ShopMagic – email automation for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.5 Although `CurrentCustomer::encode_tracking_data()` appends an md5 hash to the `shopmagic_visitor_` cookie to make it tamper-resistant, `CookiePersistence::get_tracking_data()` returns the raw `json_decode()`'d cookie value directly without computing or verifying that hash, leaving the cookie's `user_id`, `email`, and `meta` fields fully under attacker control. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to forge the visitor cookie — which is predictable because its name is derived as `md5(siteurl)` from the public site URL — and submit it to the unprotected `wp_ajax_nopriv_capture_email_url` endpoint (which is registered without a nonce check or capability check) to impersonate any WordPress user including administrators in ShopMagic's customer-identity context, and to overwrite the stored profile metadata — including name, phone number, and billing address — of any existing guest record in `wp_shopmagic_guest` and `wp_shopmagic_guest_meta` via `GuestManager::save()`.
  
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-136508 - MSDTC connections drop the connection's TLS and channel binding settings
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-136508
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 11:17 p.m. | 1 hour, 5 minutes ago
  
Description :On Windows, when a connection takes part in a distributed transaction, psqlODBC and its XA library open further connections of their own to finish the transaction. These connections did not keep the security settings of the application's connection:

- When the XA library's first connection attempt failed, it tried again with sslmode=allow, even for a data source configured with sslmode=verify-full or verify-ca.
- The connections the driver opens itself ignored every libpq option given through pqopt, such as channel_binding=require, and the open string it registers with MSDTC carried no pqopt, so the XA library's connections dropped those options too.

An attacker on the network path between the MSDTC host and the PostgreSQL server, without a certificate or credentials, can make those connections go to a server of their choosing without TLS, read and change what they send, and decide the outcome MSDTC records for the transaction.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
  
Severity: 6.8 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

Description :Crypt::JWT versions before 0.024 for Perl skip issuer, subject, audience and JWT ID checks when the claim is absent or the option is a plain string.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-136515 - Memory corruption and crashes when the driver rewrites statements for cursors and escapes
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-136515
  
Published : 2026年11月25日 22:25 | 36 分钟 ago
  
Description :psqlODBC rewrites statement text for keyset-driven cursors and ODBC escapes using positions it found in the text. These positions could lie outside the text or describe another statement:

- After SQLExecDirect() failed on a statement handle, the FROM and WHERE positions of the failed statement were applied to the next, shorter statement on that handle.
- The parser could record a FROM position with no text after it, and the rewrite then copied a negative length.
- An {fn …} escape whose arguments contain FOR UPDATE, ; or INTO … FROM made the driver remove a cursor prefix from the wrong buffer.
- {fn CONVERT(?, …)} with an output parameter produced a negative argument length.
- An unclosed {fn …} escape made the driver read past the statement, and a few thousand nested ones exhausted the stack.
- Translating @@identity in long statement text read an uninitialised pointer, and {? = call …} with nothing bound for the return value dereferenced NULL.

Whoever supplies the text of a statement that an application opens on a keyset-driven or dynamic cursor with a concurrency other than read-only, or calls with an output parameter, can corrupt the application's heap and end it. That includes the users of query tools, report builders and other applications that run SQL their users type. Code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
  
Severity: 7.5 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-134070 - Improper input validation in the AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-134070
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 7:37 p.m. | 29 minutes ago
  
Description :Improper input validation in the AWS-managed AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 might allow an authenticated remote user who is permitted to run the runbook to set unintended configuration in the account's Regional Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) via a crafted S3KeyPrefix parameter value. This applies only when that document does not already exist in the Region. The unintended configuration can include arbitrary commands, which then run on managed instances when other users start Session Manager sessions.



Because any user permitted to run the runbook selects which revision to run, this issue remains reachable in an affected Region until earlier revisions can no longer be run there. AWS is deprecating all revisions created before 2026-10-22 (UTC) in every Region and partition beginning January 15, 2027; until deprecation, earlier revisions remain runnable, so upgrading alone is not sufficient.



To remediate this issue:



1. Run the latest revision of the runbook. The latest revision is the fixed revision in every Region where the runbook is available, and its revision number varies by Region. To find it, run aws ssm describe-document --name AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 --region  --query "Document.LatestVersion". Update any Automation executions, State Manager associations, AWS Config remediation configurations, or other automations pinned to an earlier revision to use the latest revision. 2. Until earlier revisions are removed in your Region, either keep untrusted users from running earlier revisions of the runbook, or keep a trusted Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) in every Region. Earlier revisions inject only when they create this document, so while a trusted one exists, this path is closed in that Region. 3. Review your Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) in any Region where it was first created by an earlier revision of this runbook, not by you. To check, look for any run of this runbook that failed with "DOCUMENT CREATE OR UPDATE FAILED." An injected run always fails with this error. You can also compare the creation date of the document's first version with the start times of runs of this runbook in that Region. Check the document for settings you did not configure, especially shellProfile, Run As (runAsEnabled, runAsDefaultUser), maxSessionDuration, idleSessionTimeout, and the logging destination fields. The fixed runbook updates only the S3 bucket and prefix fields of an existing preferences document, so settings injected earlier remain until you remove them. If you find unexpected settings, restore your trusted preferences and review instances on which Session Manager sessions were started while those settings were active. The AWS Security Bulletin includes commands for this review.
  
Severity: 8.0 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-99811 - vfio/cdx: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99811
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 6:26 p.m. | 35 minutes ago
  
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vfio/cdx: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable

vfio_cdx_mmap() rejects writable mappings of regions without the WRITE
flag, but leaves VM_MAYWRITE set.  Userspace can map such a region
read-only and then upgrade the mapping to writable with mprotect(),
writing to MMIO regions the device marks read-only.

Clear VM_MAYWRITE for regions without the WRITE flag, as i915 does for
its read-only objects and as fixed in drm/vc4 (CVE-2026-68445),
drm/panthor (CVE-2024-53071) and commit a5edadbae57e ("ptp: vmclock:
prevent read-only mappings from becoming writable").

Note this is defensive hardening: no in-tree cdx device currently
publishes a region without the WRITE flag.  The guard costs nothing and
keeps the mmap() interface honest if a read-only region ever appears.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-135150 - Eclipse Ditto Authentication Bypass via Header Injection
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-135150
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 3:49 p.m. | 31 minutes ago
  
Description :In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.9, the nginx reverse proxy configurations shipped with Ditto (Helm chart, Docker Compose, Kubernetes and OpenShift deployment files) forward a client-supplied

  `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` header to the Ditto gateway on locations that do not apply nginx authentication, such as `/api/2/connections`. nginx selects the location based on the normalized request URI
  but forwards the raw URI, while the gateway does not treat an encoded slash (`%2f`) as a path separator. A crafted request path is therefore routed by nginx through such an unauthenticated location and
  by the gateway to the regular Things and Policies HTTP API, including routes that send live messages to devices. When pre-authentication is enabled (the default of the Helm chart and the Docker Compose
  setup), an unauthenticated remote attacker can impersonate arbitrary policy subjects and read, modify and delete Things, read Policies, send messages to devices and create entities. Additionally, the
  optional Ingress of the Helm chart (Ditto 3.9.0 to 3.9.9) routes requests directly to the gateway without setting or removing that header, and the WebSocket Ingress of the Helm chart of Ditto 3.3.0 to
  3.8.15 does not set it, allowing the same impersonation without path manipulation when pre-authentication is enabled. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-120753.
  
Severity: 9.1 | CRITICAL
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2024-7430 - Bypass Separation of Duties in Opentext Application Performance Management
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2024-7430
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 12:05 p.m. | 26 minutes ago
  
Description :Application Performance Management 9.60 patch versions before IP4 are affected. This issue seems to be present throughout the application, as several endpoints or functionalities that are restricted to Admin users can be directly accessed by Regular users. The authorization method of the application can be bypassed allowing users to perform unauthorized actions to their role. The application supports different levels of access. The application performs authorization checks to keep users from accessing functionality outside of their role such as create, verify, and/or repair. 




This authorization method can be bypassed. During VA testing, it was found that under the User Reports inside the Applications menu, it is possible to  create links and different reports. However, the creation of custom links, Excel reports, and service reports are restricted to admin users. Hence, it is possible for regular users with the least privileges to directly access these 

pages and the application allows them to further use these restricted functionalities.
  
Severity: 8.4 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CISA Adds 10 Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
vulnerability.summary:
CISA has added 10 new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

CVE-2023-25914 Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series Path Traversal Vulnerability
CVE-2023-25915 Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series Improper Input Validation Vulnerability 
CVE-2025-41450 Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series Improper Authentication Vulnerability 
CVE-2026-103406 Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router OS Command Injection Vulnerability 
CVE-2026-133275 Mitel MiCollab Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type Vulnerability 
CVE-2026-133303 Mitel MiCollab XML Injection Vulnerability 
CVE-2026-133311 Mitel MiCollab Weak Authentication Vulnerability 
CVE-2026-133323 Mitel MiCollab OS Command Injection Vulnerability 
CVE-2026-133324 Mitel MiCollab Not Failing Securely Vulnerability 
CVE-2026-133469 Vates Xen Orchestra Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input Vulnerability 



These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.


Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.


While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.


Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-134792 - HttpClient Lets the Proxy Header of a Request Choose the Proxy of Outgoing Requests in HTTP Workers That Run Under the CLI SAPI
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-134792
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 10 a.m. | 19 minutes ago
  
Description :When the proxy option isn't set, HttpClient takes the proxy from environment variables like http_proxy or HTTP_PROXY. On web servers, it ignores HTTP_PROXY, because PHP puts the Proxy request header there (the httpoxy issue). On the CLI SAPI, it read HTTP_PROXY from $_SERVER, where PHP also puts the environment.

HTTP workers that run under the CLI SAPI put the headers of each request in $_SERVER too. This is the case of spiral/roadrunner-http, which the RoadRunner runner of php-runtime uses, and of baldinof/roadrunner-bundle and php-pm. A client could then send a Proxy header to choose the proxy of the requests that the application sent while handling its request. That proxy received the full requests to http:// URLs, with their credentials, and could forge the responses. For https:// URLs, it learned the host and port through CONNECT.

NativeHttpClient is affected since Symfony 4.3.0, AmpHttpClient since 5.1.0, and CurlHttpClient since 4.4.40, 5.4.7 and 6.0.7.

On the CLI SAPI, HTTP_PROXY is now read from the environment with $_ENV and getenv(), never from $_SERVER. Other SAPIs still ignore it.
  
Severity: 8.3 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-134791 - Unclosed Comments Make the Lexer of ExpressionLanguage Quadratic, Letting Untrusted Expressions Hold a Process
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-134791
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 10 a.m. | 19 minutes ago
  
Description :Since Symfony 7.2, expressions can contain comments. The lexer used a regular expression to find the end of a comment. When a /* was never closed, this regular expression scanned the rest of the expression, and the lexer then went on with the next character. So each /* scanned the rest of the expression again. Linting 192 KB of /*  took 9 to 11 seconds, and 96 KB took 34 seconds without PCRE JIT.

The lexer runs before the parser and its nesting limit. Any code that lints or parses untrusted expressions is affected, including the ExpressionSyntax validation constraint. A Length constraint on the same value doesn't help, since the validator runs both constraints.

The lexer now uses strpos() to find the end of a comment, and a comment that is never closed throws a SyntaxError. Such expressions were already invalid. Lexing takes linear time again.
  
Severity: 8.7 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133756 - HtmlSanitizer Doesn't Check Meta Refresh URLs Whose Time Follows a Vertical Tab or a Unicode Space: Incomplete Fix for CVE-2026-121373
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133756
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 10 a.m. | 19 minutes ago
  
Description :MetaRefreshAttributeSanitizer checks the URL of a  directive only when its content starts with a refresh time. Since the fix for CVE-2026-121373, only the ASCII whitespace of the HTML specification could come before that time. Chromium-based browsers also skip a vertical tab and the Unicode spaces U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+205F and U+3000.

When the time followed one of these characters, the sanitizer returned the value unchanged. Its URL wasn't checked against allowLinkHosts() and allowLinkSchemes(), and Chromium followed it:

$sanitizer->sanitizeFor('head', "");
// returned unchanged, and Chromium redirects to https://evil.example/

The vertical tab is a regression of the fix for CVE-2026-121373, since the expression used before matched it. The Unicode spaces have been accepted since the sanitizer of meta refresh directives exists.

This requires the configuration of CVE-2026-121373: meta elements allowed with their http-equiv and content attributes, for example with allowStaticElements(), and content sanitized with sanitizeFor('head', ...). Firefox and Safari skip only ASCII whitespace there.

The sanitizer now skips controls, Unicode whitespace and invisible characters before the time, so that it checks the URL of these directives too.
  
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133753 - The Unanimous Strategy Grants access_control Rules When Only One of Their Roles Matches: Regression of CVE-2020-5275
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133753
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 10 a.m. | 19 minutes ago
  
Description :With the unanimous access decision strategy, an access_control rule that lists several roles requires all of them. That's the behavior restored by the fix for CVE-2020-5275. Since Symfony 5.4, the access decision manager asked each voter once about all the attributes of a rule. RoleVoter grants access as soon as the user has one of the roles. So a user who had only one of these roles was granted access:

security:
    access_decision_manager:
        strategy: unanimous
    access_control:
- { path: ^/admin, roles: [ROLE_ADMIN, ROLE_AUDITOR] }

Only attributes decided by the same voter were affected. For example, a role combined with allow_if still required both.

With the unanimous strategy, voters are asked about each attribute separately again, as before Symfony 5.4. Access is denied as soon as one of the attributes is denied.
  
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133749 - Programmatic Logins With Guard Skip the checkPostAuth() Method of User Checkers
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133749
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 10 a.m. | 19 minutes ago
  
Description :GuardAuthenticatorHandler::authenticateUserAndHandleSuccess() logs a user in programmatically with a Guard authenticator, for example in the registration controllers that MakerBundle generated. This method creates the token and stores it, but it calls neither checkPreAuth() nor checkPostAuth() on the user checker of the firewall. Guard authenticators run both checks when they authenticate a request.

As a consequence, an account that a user checker rejects in checkPostAuth() could still be logged in through this method, for example an expired account.

Applications are affected when they use Guard with a custom user checker that rejects users in checkPostAuth(), and log users in with authenticateUserAndHandleSuccess(). The default user checker also rejects users of the deprecated User class whose credentials expired. This is the issue of GHSA-8f57-m8wj-x65w, for the Guard component of Symfony 5.4. Guard was removed in Symfony 6.0.

GuardAuthenticatorHandler::authenticateUserAndHandleSuccess() now calls the checkPostAuth() method of the user checker of the firewall before it stores the token. AuthenticatorManager::authenticateUser() does the same since the fix for GHSA-8f57-m8wj-x65w. Like authenticateUser(), authenticateUserAndHandleSuccess() doesn't call checkPreAuth(). Programmatic logins skip this check on purpose, for example right after a registration. SecurityBundle now gives the user checkers of the firewalls to the handler, so both symfony/security-guard and symfony/security-bundle must be updated.

As a consequence, an exception thrown by checkPostAuth() now comes out of authenticateUserAndHandleSuccess(). Code that logs users in programmatically may need to catch it.
  
Severity: 2.3 | LOW
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-136641 - PlaywrightBrowser's egress policy does not cover WebRTC, WebTransport, WebSocketStream or FedCM traffic
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-136641
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 9:39 a.m. | 27 minutes ago
  
Description :Pydantic AI Harness's PlaywrightBrowser enforces its egress policy on HTTP requests and page WebSockets, but not on WebRTC or WebTransport connections, WebSockets opened with WebSocketStream, or the requests the browser itself sends for FedCM. A page the agent opens can make the browser send WebRTC (STUN and TURN), WebTransport and WebSocketStream traffic, and FedCM requests, to hosts and ports that the policy refuses, including under a policy that limits every request kind to an allowlist.

This affects applications that use PlaywrightBrowser to open pages an attacker can influence. The traffic is each protocol's connection setup, sent to a destination the page chooses. A page can learn whether a target answers a STUN request. No response body from an ordinary internal service was readable through WebRTC, WebTransport or FedCM. A WebSocketStream is an ordinary WebSocket that the WebSocket guard does not see, opened from a page, a frame or a worker, and the page reads what the server sends, including from a private address. Chromium's Local Network Access blocks WebTransport from public pages to private addresses, but does not block WebRTC.

A FedCM call (navigator.credentials.get with an identity provider) makes the browser fetch the provider's /.well-known/web-identity, config, accounts and client metadata URLs. The page chooses the config URL's path and the client ID, so it can send data to a host outside allowed_domains or listed in blocked_domains. The accounts request carries the provider's cookies from the browser profile. FedCM requires a provider origin that is HTTPS or loopback.

The assumed attacker is a third party with no access to the application who controls script on a page the agent opens.

Under an enforced egress policy, which is the default, pydantic-ai-harness 0.74.0 removes RTCPeerConnection, webkitRTCPeerConnection, WebTransport, WebSocketStream, IdentityCredential and IdentityProvider from every page and frame, refuses FedCM calls to navigator.credentials.get, and launches Chromium with FedCM and WebSocketStream turned off. These paths stay outside the policy: WebTransport from workers; WebSocketStream from workers in a browser reached over cdp_url; WebTransport in sandboxed iframes that Chromium runs in their own process (headless=False and cdp_url); and documents loaded before attachment under cdp_context='default'.

Upgrade pydantic-ai-harness to 0.74.0 or later. For the paths the upgrade leaves open, and until you upgrade, run the browser behind a network egress filter that also covers UDP, or do not open untrusted URLs with PlaywrightBrowser.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-134875 - GV-EBD4700 Series Default HTTPS private key
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-134875
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 12:29 a.m. | 48 minutes ago
  
Description :An unencrypted RSA private key for a default HTTPS certificate is included in GeoVision GV-EBD4700 firmware V1.11 (A02-GV-EBD4700_V1.11_2026_10_13.zip) at /program/www/ssl_cert.pem and copied to /config/ssl_cert.pem during initialization. When HTTPS is enabled using the default certificate, a network on-path attacker who obtains the firmware image can use the exposed private key to present an identical certificate and intercept HTTPS traffic. HTTPS is disabled by default .


  *  

Only impacts deployments where an administrator enables HTTPS and retains the default certificate. Because the private key is publicly distributed in the firmware image, an on-path attacker can impersonate the device with an identical certificate fingerprint, bypassing fingerprint checks and stored certificate exceptions (potentially capturing credentials if a user clicks through the expired-certificate warning).

CVE ID :CVE-2026-16669
  
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 12:17 a.m. | 15 minutes ago
  
Description :MCUboot's Espressif port omits zeroization of two sensitive stack buffers in boot/espressif/hal/src/flash_encrypt.c. In check_and_generate_encryption_keys(), the freshly generated XTS-AES flash-encryption key is held in the stack array keys[BLOCKS_NEEDED][32] (flash_encrypt.c:216), written to eFuse via esp_efuse_write_keys(), and the function returns (flash_encrypt.c:243) without scrubbing it. In esp_flash_encrypt_region(), the plaintext flash sector buffer buf (flash_encrypt.c:454) retains the last sector's cleartext at both the success and flash_failed returns. Neither path performs a memset/bzero/mbedtls_platform_zeroize, even though the same port already does bzero for key digests in boot/espressif/hal/src/secure_boot.c.

The affected code runs only on the Espressif port with CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED, and only during the one-time first-boot provisioning pass when flash encryption is not yet enabled (boot/espressif/main.c); on subsequent boots the buffers are never created. Recovering the residue requires an out-of-band stack/RAM-disclosure primitive — JTAG/debug halt, UART ROM download, a core/crash dump, or a warm-boot RAM scrape — captured during that single provisioning boot. Under the recommended CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_RELEASE plus secure boot, those channels are fused off and no exposure exists.

The practical impact is a low-severity, defense-in-depth hardening gap: a flash-encryption key (and last plaintext sector) may linger in bootloader stack memory. Because the eFuse key block is burned read+write-protected, the transient stack copy is the only readable copy, and only during one boot; in a development build where a disclosure channel is open, an attacker with that capability can usually already read the still-plaintext flash directly, so the marginal confidentiality gain is small. Confirming real-world recovery depends on a specific SoC/debug configuration not exercisable from source alone.
  
Severity: 2.0 | LOW

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-16668 - Unbounded CBOR recursion in MCUboot serial recovery allows pre-authentication stack exhaustion
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-16668
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 10:39 p.m. | 41 minutes ago
  
Description :The vendored zcbor decoder's zcbor_any_skip() in boot/zcbor/src/zcbor_decode.c descends one C-stack frame per level of CBOR nesting. On a list or map it copies the decoder state (memcpy(&state_copy, state, sizeof(zcbor_state_t))) and recurses once per member, with no depth cap: the skip path does not use zcbor's backup stack, and ZCBOR_MAX_ELEM_COUNT is SIZE_MAX, so nothing bounds how deep the recursion goes.

That function is reached on attacker-controlled bytes before any authentication. MCUboot's serial-recovery command parser decodes SMP/CBOR requests with zcbor_map_decode_bulk() (boot/boot_serial/src/zcbor_bulk.c), which skips any map key it does not recognise by calling zcbor_any_skip() on the encoded value; the echo handler in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c calls it directly on the same footing. Both run during image upload, long before the uploaded image's signature is checked. The default receive buffer is MCUBOOT_SERIAL_MAX_RECEIVE_SIZE = 512 bytes and each nesting level costs a single byte to encode (0x81), so roughly 500 levels of nesting fit in one request — comfortably more than a bootloader's stack can absorb, since every frame carries a full zcbor_state_t copy plus locals.

The impact is availability only: the bootloader's stack overflows and the device faults or hangs during recovery. There is no controlled out-of-bounds write that escapes the DFU buffer, no disclosure, and no authentication bypass — the recursion grows the stack with the decoder's own internal state. Whether a given board actually exhausts its stack depends on that board's bootloader stack size, which we did not measure; the fix is nevertheless unconditional, because an unauthenticated pre-authentication code path must not have its safety depend on a per-board stack margin.

Exposure requires MCUBOOT_SERIAL (serial/SMP recovery), which is not enabled by default, and recovery entry is normally gated on a physical pin (CONFIG_BOOT_SERIAL_ENTRANCE_GPIO / PIN_RESET), with a no-valid-image fallback path. Products that expose serial recovery over an externally reachable transport, or that fall into recovery when no valid image is present, are the ones at risk.

The fix is to bound the skip: thread a recursion-depth counter through zcbor_any_skip() (or have zcbor_map_decode_bulk() reject values nested beyond a small constant) and fail once the limit is exceeded — equivalently, take the bounded-skip implementation from upstream zcbor.
  
Severity: 2.4 | LOW

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-16665 - MCUboot uses assert() as a security guard on the boot/swap/validation path; under NDEBUG (release builds) these checks are compiled out, so an inconsistent/attacker-influenced swap status is not aborted and the swap completes on bad state
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-16665
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 9:39 p.m. | 48 minutes ago
  
Description :Summary

MCUboot enforces several security-critical invariants on the boot, image-swap, and validation paths using assert(). In a standard release/production build (NDEBUG defined) assert() expands to a no-op, so an invariant the code intends to halt on instead falls through, and execution continues with the bad or inconsistent state. Where the guarded condition is attacker-influenceable through the flash-write boundary (serial-recovery / DFU), this is a security check that is simply absent in release builds.

This is one root cause (assert-as-security-guard, no-op under NDEBUG) with one fix approach (replace the security-critical asserts with real fail-closed checks), so it is filed as a single advisory covering the enumerated sites.

Worst reachable instance — inconsistent swap status completes the swap without validation

In the swap-resume status read, an inconsistent status (erased_sections > 1) is detected, logged, and — when MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT is disabled — is meant to abort, because "there is no way to be sure the swapped primary slot is OK." The abort is assert(0):

boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:181-194 — if (erased_sections > 1) { ... #if !defined(MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT) / ... abort! / assert(0); #endif }, then execution falls through to compute bs->op/idx/state from the inconsistent status (lines 197-208) and return 0 (success).
boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:266-280 — identical pattern; falls through to bs->op/idx/state and return 0.
boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:227-241 — same invalid/assert(0) pattern for the scratch backend.

Under NDEBUG with primary-slot validation off, the inconsistent status is neither aborted (assert is a no-op) nor re-validated (validation off), so boot_complete_partial_swap() finishes the swap on inconsistent metadata and the primary slot is booted without a signature check. An attacker who can write the swap-status trailer can craft the inconsistent status.

Reachability (threat model). Secondary slot + scratch trailers are A2-writable by definition (that is what a DFU upload is). Under MCUBOOT_SERIAL_RECOVERY the primary trailer is A2-writable too: boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:978 opens flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot(img_num, 0) (== primary) and writes from offset 0 bounded by area_size, so it can paint the primary swap-status/magic. This is how the A2 (recovery/DFU, unauthenticated by design) attacker influences the guarded condition. Property violated: P1 (image authenticity / secure-boot bypass) when un-revalidated content is booted, and P6 (boot/recovery availability).

Second reachable instance — resume-path swap_size from an unguarded trailer

boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1190-1193: the swap resume branch does fap = boot_find_status(...); assert(fap != NULL); rc = boot_read_swap_size(fap, &bs->swap_size); assert(rc == 0);. boot_find_status() (boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_misc.c:166-204) searches {scratch, primary} and, on no-valid-magic-match, returns the last-iterated area (primary), not NULL — so assert(fap != NULL) cannot fire even in debug, and under NDEBUG neither assert fires. swap_size is then read from an A2-writable (serial-recovery primary, or scratch) trailer with no fail-closed handling. This is the same swap-metadata-trust family as the recorded resume/swap_size disclosure.

Reachable-security sites (center the fix here)

1. boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:193 — inconsistent-status assert(0), falls through to complete swap. A2 + !VALIDATE_PRIMARY. [worst]
2. boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:278 — same, swap-offset backend.
3. boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:239 — same, swap-scratch backend.
4. boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1191 and :1193 — resume assert(fap != NULL) / assert(rc == 0) guarding swap_size read from an A2-writable trailer; compounded by boot_find_status() never returning NULL.

(Truncated. The full description is in the advisory: https://github.com/mcu-tools/mcuboot/security/advisories/GHSA-cr9j-p626-pwcc)
  
Severity: 7.4 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-16663 - Pre-authentication out-of-bounds write in MCUboot encrypted serial recovery image decryption
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-16663
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 9:39 p.m. | 48 minutes ago
  
Description :MCUboot's encrypted serial-recovery path contains an attacker-controlled out-of-bounds stack write in decrypt_region_inplace() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c. The routine decrypts an uploaded encrypted image one flash sector at a time into a sector-sized stack VLA buf[sz], but when the current sector is still inside the image header it sets the destination index to the absolute header size (idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size; at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:156) and then decrypts into &buf[idx]. The correct sibling routine boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:876 uses the sector-relative idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size - abs_off; the serial path is missing the - abs_off term, so for any sector after the first the index runs past the end of the stack buffer.

The ih_hdr_size field is a uint16_t taken verbatim from the uploaded image header. On the second sector onward, when ih_hdr_size exceeds the sector size, &buf[idx] points beyond buf and boot_enc_decrypt() writes attacker-controlled plaintext into adjacent stack frames. The path is reached pre-authentication: bs_upload() calls boot_handle_enc_fw() (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:1208) after upload, and the pre-decryption signature gate in decrypt_image_inplace() is compiled out (#if 0 at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:226-233), so the header is never validated before decryption.

A second error in the same window computation affects the first sector. When a sector holds both the end of the header and the start of the TLV area, the decrypt length is clamped to tlv_off - (off + bytes_copied), measured from the start of the sector rather than from idx (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:166). An encrypted image whose header and payload end within the first sector is therefore decrypted for ih_hdr_size bytes more than it should be: into the TLV area and, when the image ends near the end of the sector, past buf. This form needs no oversized header, so even an ordinary small encrypted image can trigger it, and it reaches devices with sectors of up to about 128 KiB rather than only those whose sector is smaller than the 16-bit ih_hdr_size.

Reaching the sink requires a build with MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES and serial recovery enabled, and access to the device's serial/USB recovery interface (unauthenticated by design). With the public-key encryption schemes the AES content key is wrapped to the device's public encryption key, so an attacker can author a fully crafted encrypted image — including a malicious ih_hdr_size — without the image-signing private key. The result is a controllable stack memory-corruption inside the bootloader before any signature check, providing a path to code execution in the secure-boot root of trust that bypasses image authentication, as well as a denial-of-service. A 2048-byte out-of-bounds write was reproduced under AddressSanitizer (sz=4096, off=4096, ih_hdr_size=6144).

On releases before v2.0.0 (v1.9.0 and v1.10.0) the destination is a file-scope static uint8_t buf[SOC_FLASH_ERASE_BLK_SZ] in .bss rather than the stack VLA described above — the code then lived in boot/zephyr/single_loader.c, before commit c9fa6088 relocated it to boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c and changed the buffer's storage class. The out-of-bounds write is equally real and equally pre-authentication on those releases, but it corrupts adjacent static data rather than the stack, so a stack-smashing proof of concept written against a current release will not reproduce as-is there.
  
Severity: 8.4 | HIGH

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-135479 - Merchant for WooCommerce before 2.3.3 Missing Authorization via Quick View AJAX
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-135479
  
Published : 24 de Novembro de 2026 às 15:34 | 22 minutos ago
  
Description :Merchant for WooCommerce before 2.3.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Quick View module that allows unauthenticated attackers to read draft, pending, private, and scheduled WooCommerce products. The modal_content_ajax_callback() handler for the merchant_quick_view_content AJAX action is registered for unauthenticated users, is gated only by the merchant-nonce value exposed to every front-end visitor, and loads any supplied product_id with wc_get_product() without checking the product's post status or the user's read_post capability. Attackers can iterate product IDs to obtain the title, price, description, gallery images, and SKU of unpublished products when the Quick View module is enabled.

vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-115747
  
Published : 24 de Novembro de 2026 às 15:29 | 27 minutos ago
  
Description :Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer vulnerability in the AArch64 JIT in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker to crash the BEAM virtual machine via input that reaches a chained integer range guard, such as an oversized numeric character reference parsed by xmerl_sax_parser.

In erts/emulator/beam/jit/arm/instr_common.cpp, BeamModuleAssembler::emit_is_ge_lt wraps its generated code in preserve_cache and marks only TMP1 as clobbered. When the compared value is not a small integer, the generated code calls the shared fragment is_ge_lt_shared, which also overwrites ARG1 and other caller-saved registers. The register cache keeps stale entries, so later instructions may use a clobbered register as an Erlang term and the emulator dies with a segmentation fault. A reference such as � takes this path in the ?is_char guard of the SAX parser. Only AArch64 builds that run the JIT are affected. The x86-64 JIT and interpreter builds do not contain the faulty code.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 27.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 15.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-65621 - Unvalidated object metadata in ex_aws_s3 enables HTTP header (CRLF) injection into S3 requests
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-65621
  
Published : 24 de Novembro de 2026 às 15:17 | 38 minutos ago
  
Description :ex_aws_s3 builds x-amz-meta-* request headers by interpolating user-supplied object metadata directly into header names and values without any validation. In ExAws.S3.Utils.build_meta_headers/1 (lib/ex_aws/s3/utils.ex), each :meta entry is turned into a header as {"x-amz-meta-#{k}", v} with no check for carriage return (CR), line feed (LF), or other illegal header bytes.

Object metadata is routinely derived from end-user input (for example an upload service that lets users attach a comment or label to an object). When such input reaches ExAws.S3.put_object/4 or any other operation accepting the :meta option, a value containing CR/LF is carried unchanged into the outbound header list. If the configured HTTP adapter does not neutralize header values before writing them to the socket, the embedded CRLF starts a new header line, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary headers into (or split) the HTTP request the library sends to the S3 endpoint. This is an HTTP header (CRLF) injection leading to HTTP request splitting. The practical impact depends on the HTTP adapter, and no authentication is required beyond the ability to influence object metadata.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.
  
Severity: 2.1 | LOW
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-136158 - Valkey JSON: Use-after-free in array mutation commands through a recursive JSONPath
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-136158
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 3:17 p.m. | 13 minutes ago
  
Description :In Valkey JSON 1.0.0 through 1.0.2, a recursive JSONPath expression such as $..* returns both an array and elements nested inside it. The size-changing mutators (JSON.ARRAPPEND, JSON.ARRINSERT, JSON.ARRPOP, JSON.ARRTRIM and JSON.CLEAR) process the ancestor first, which can reallocate its element buffer and free the old storage while the descendant entries in the result set still point into it; the module then writes through those dangling pointers. An authenticated user who can run these commands can use this to reliably crash the server, and it has been developed into remote code execution as the user the server runs as. Servers that do not load the JSON module, including through valkey-bundle, are not affected.
  
Severity: 8.8 | HIGH

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-62271 - ex_aws_kms defaults RSA key-material wrapping to PKCS#1 v1.5 in get_parameters_for_import/3
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-62271
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 12:22 p.m. | 30 minutes ago
  
Description :Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_kms (ExAws.KMS module) causes callers who import external key material to wrap their secret KMS key material with the deprecated PKCS#1 v1.5 padding scheme by default.

This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/kms.ex and program routine ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3.

ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3 defaults its wrapping_algorithm argument to "RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5". AWS KMS returns this value as the WrappingAlgorithm for the import operation, and it dictates the RSA padding scheme the caller uses to wrap (RSA-encrypt) their secret key material before calling ImportKeyMaterial. AWS KMS also supports the stronger RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1 and RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256 schemes. By defaulting to RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5, the library steers callers who do not explicitly override the argument toward the weakest of the three. PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption padding is susceptible to Bleichenbacher adaptive chosen-ciphertext (padding oracle) attacks, which can recover the wrapped plaintext without the private key given an oracle that reveals whether a decrypted value was validly padded. Because the unwrap happens inside AWS KMS, which does not expose a padding oracle, the practical exploitability is low and this is a defense-in-depth weakness. Callers can avoid the weak default by explicitly passing "RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256" (or "RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1") as the wrapping algorithm.

This issue affects ex_aws_kms: from 2.1.0 before 2.7.0.
  
Severity: 2.1 | LOW
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

Recommended Practices
CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-84785 - Unbounded Out-of-Order Fragment Reassembly in QUIC Streams
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-84785
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 11:30 a.m. | 49 minutes ago
  
Description :Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small out-of-order STREAM fragments
while withholding the first byte of the stream may cause OpenSSL to buffer
a large number of reassembly nodes occupying much larger memory than
the actual data sent.

Impact summary: A remote peer can pin large amounts of memory on a server that
accepts incoming QUIC streams, potentially exhausting memory and causing
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: QUIC receive flow control limits the highest byte offset a peer
may reach on a stream. It does not limit how many out-of-order fragments the
receiver buffers. OpenSSL allocates a reassembly node for each non-adjacent
STREAM fragment and never caps the count. A peer that opens a stream and sends
many one-byte fragments at increasing offsets, while withholding the first
byte, makes the receiver retain one node per fragment without delivering any
data.

Only applications that accept incoming streams are exposed. With the default
policy, which rejects peer-initiated streams, the stream is torn down before
state accumulates. Because the read side never advances past the missing
prefix, the flow control window never slides and the nodes stay pinned for the
life of the connection.

The per-stream window bounds the highest offset, so the memory one stream can
pin is finite, but it can reach tens of megabytes and, across many streams and
connections, drive memory pressure and Denial of Service. The severity is
limited because the exhaustion is bounded by flow control and requires a
non-default configuration.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-82446 - Apache StormCrawler: Server-Side Request Forgery and Cross-Origin Credential Disclosure via robots.txt Redirect Handling
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-82446
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 11:17 a.m. | 13 minutes ago
  
Description :Description

When StormCrawler fetches a host's `/robots.txt` and receives a redirect, `HttpRobotRulesParser`
resolves the `Location` header and re-fetches the target for up to five hops. The loop checks neither
the scheme, the host nor the port of the resolved target, and it is not governed by
`http.allow.redirects`, which only affects the page fetch. A crawled site can therefore point the
robots.txt fetch at any address reachable from the fetcher worker, including loopback interfaces,
private ranges and cloud metadata endpoints. Every crawled URL triggers a robots.txt fetch on a cache
miss, so no unusual configuration is required to reach the loop.

The fetched body is only parsed as robots rules and is not returned to the caller, so the read itself
is blind. The more direct impact is on credentials: the okhttp protocol applies its configured request
headers, including the `Authorization` header built from `http.basicauth.user` and
`http.basicauth.password` and anything in `http.custom.headers`, to every request it makes. Because
StormCrawler follows the redirect itself and issues a new request, okhttp's own removal of the
`Authorization` header across a host change does not apply, and the operator's crawl credentials are
delivered to the host the redirect names.

The connection-time IP filter, `http.filter.ipaddress.include` and `http.filter.ipaddress.exclude`, is
installed as an okhttp network interceptor on the same client and does apply to these hops when it is
configured. It ships with no rules, which is why the path is reachable in a default configuration. URL
filtering never applies, because the robots.txt fetch does not pass through the outlink filter chain.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 4.0.0, where a robots.txt redirect is followed only when the target uses http or https and
shares scheme, host and port with the URL it was reached from. Deployments that legitimately serve
robots.txt through a cross-host redirect can restore the previous behaviour with
`http.robots.redirect.crosshost.allow`.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should set `http.filter.ipaddress.exclude` to cover loopback,
private, link-local and CGNAT ranges, which is enforced after DNS resolution and therefore also on
redirect hops. Operators who configure `http.basicauth.*` or `http.custom.headers` for a crawl should
assume those credentials may have been sent to third-party hosts and rotate them, and should scope
credentials by running a separate topology per origin.

Credit

Independently reported to the Apache StormCrawler PMC by n0mi1k, with a proof of concept.

Also found by the ASF -- using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated
and reported by Apache StormCrawler.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-135804 - Incomplete Fix for CVE-2026-45756: JsonPath Queries Can Still Hold a Process Through search(), match() and Chained Filters
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-135804
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 8:55 a.m. | 31 minutes ago
  
Description :The fix for CVE-2026-45756 lowers pcre.backtrack_limit to 10000 around each preg_match() call of the match() and search() filter functions. That limit applies to one starting position, not to one call. PCRE resets its counter at every position it tries a match from. So an unanchored pattern that stays just under the limit is paid once per byte of the subject. Each call also starts from a fresh limit, so chaining clauses in one filter multiplies the work.

Two other paths made the cost of a query grow faster than its size, without any regular expression:
- The filter evaluator scanned the whole expression for logical operators once per node. Its cost grew with the square of the number of chained clauses.
- Queries starting with $ inside a filter, like @.x == $.limit or length($.items), were evaluated again for every node the filter visits.

An application that evaluates an attacker-influenced JSONPath expression can therefore still be made to hold a PHP worker. A document of 2 MB and a query of 2.5 KB take 3.5 minutes of CPU.

JsonCrawler::find() now bounds the total regex work of one call, and throws an exception when that budget is exhausted. Filter expressions are parsed once per query, and absolute queries inside filters are evaluated once per query.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-135803 - Filesystem Path Treats Any Prefix Before "://" as a Root, Letting Paths Escape Their Base Directory
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-135803
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 8:55 a.m. | 31 minutes ago
  
Description :Most methods of Symfony\Component\Filesystem\Path rely on Path::split(), which takes everything before the first :// as the root of a path. It doesn't check that this prefix is a URI scheme, so the .. segments in that prefix are never resolved. PHP sees a scheme only at the start of a string. So /base/../x://../secret.txt is a plain local path to /secret.txt for PHP, while Path::isBasePath('/base', '/base/../x://../secret.txt') returns true. canonicalize(), join(), makeAbsolute() and makeRelative() are affected the same way.

Some applications check a path built from user input with isBasePath() or canonicalize(), and then open it. They can be made to read or write files outside the expected directory.

On Symfony 6.4 and later, the AssetMapper component builds with Path::join() the path of the files that a remote package references from its CSS. A malicious or compromised package can therefore make importmap:require or importmap:install write a file of its choice outside assets/vendor. For example, the CSS url(../../../../../public/x://shell.php) writes public/x:/shell.php.

A prefix is now a scheme only when PHP would look for a stream wrapper with that name. That is two or more letters, digits, +, - or ., followed by :// at the start of the path. Other prefixes are regular path segments, and the .. segments after them are resolved. Real schemes such as phar://, file://, vfs:// or compress.zlib:// keep working.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133780 - @symfony/stimulus-bridge lazy-controller-loader: arbitrary code execution via unsanitized Stimulus magic comments
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133780
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 8:41 a.m. | 45 minutes ago
  
Description :The @symfony/stimulus-bridge npm package includes a Webpack loader called lazy-controller-loader that supports "magic comments" placed above a Stimulus controller import, for example /* stimulusFetch: 'lazy' */, to control lazy loading behavior. To read those options, the loader extracted the raw text of any stimulus* comment and evaluated it as JavaScript using Node's vm.runInNewContext(). The Node.js node:vm module is not a security sandbox, and a crafted comment can break out of the VM context using well-known techniques to run arbitrary Node.js code within the build process.

This is a build-time vulnerability: it does not affect browsers or end users. The code executes on the developer machine or CI/build server during a Webpack or Symfony Encore build. Realistic attack vectors include a malicious Stimulus controller introduced through a compromised dependency, or a pull request that triggers an automated CI build. An attacker who can get such a file into the build can read files and environment variables available to the build process, exfiltrate CI secrets, tamper with generated build artifacts, and run commands with the permissions of the build user.

The loader no longer evaluates comment content as JavaScript. It now parses each comment as an object expression using a real JavaScript parser and extracts only plain literal values. Any non-literal value, such as a function call, an identifier, or a sequence expression, is rejected and reported as a build error instead of being executed. Legitimate option values like 'lazy' and 'eager' continue to work without any changes required on the user's side.
  
Severity: 7.3 | HIGH

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-133779 - XSS in symfony/ux-icons via Attribute Names That the Sanitizer Reads Differently Than Browsers: Incomplete Fix for CVE-2026-55877
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133779
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 8:24 a.m. | 27 minutes ago
  
Description :The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. The checks matched attribute names as written in the icon, while browsers and the renderer read some names differently.

On 2.x, fromFile() keys the attributes of the root  element by their local name. A handler like x:onload passed the check, and was then rendered as onload, which runs on load. HTML parsers also read attribute names case-insensitively, so a SMIL animation with ATTRIBUTENAME="href" could set a javascript: URL on a link. And an href in the XLink namespace under another prefix, like q:href, wasn't checked. On 3.x, the sanitizer writes it out as xlink:href, and XML parsers resolve the prefix on both branches.

Applications are exposed when an attacker can influence the SVG of the icons they render. The sources are the same as for CVE-2026-55877, like local icon files and the responses of the Iconify API.

The sanitizer now checks attributes by local name. It also finds the attributeName of animations in any case, and ignores the prefix of its value.
  
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

CVE ID :CVE-2026-133779
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 8:24 a.m. | 27 minutes ago
  
Description :The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. The checks matched attribute names as written in the icon, while browsers and the renderer read some names differently.

On 2.x, fromFile() keys the attributes of the root  element by their local name. A handler like x:onload passed the check, and was then rendered as onload, which runs on load. HTML parsers also read attribute names case-insensitively, so a SMIL animation with ATTRIBUTENAME="href" could set a javascript: URL on a link. And an href in the XLink namespace under another prefix, like q:href, wasn't checked. On 3.x, the sanitizer writes it out as xlink:href, and XML parsers resolve the prefix on both branches.

Applications are exposed when an attacker can influence the SVG of the icons they render. The sources are the same as for CVE-2026-55877, like local icon files and the responses of the Iconify API.

The sanitizer now checks attributes by local name. It also finds the attributeName of animations in any case, and ignores the prefix of its value.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-105430 - NetBird relay server decodes unauthenticated Hello handshake data with gob before verifying the HMAC signature
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-105430
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 7:50 a.m. | 30 minutes ago
  
Description :Deserialization of untrusted data in the relay server handshake of NetBird versions 0.29.0 through 0.74.7 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to reach the Go encoding/gob decoder with attacker-supplied bytes before any credential is checked, which can lead to denial of service of the relay server. The deprecated Hello handshake message was still accepted before authentication and its token was decoded with gob.NewDecoder (shared/relay/auth/hmac) before the HMAC signature was verified. The handshake buffer limits the input to 212 bytes and the pre-authentication phase to 10 seconds, so there is no impact on confidentiality or integrity and the impact on availability depends on a separate weakness in the gob decoder of the Go toolchain used to build the relay server, such as CVE-2024-34156. The Auth handshake, used by clients since version 0.29.1, does not use gob. The issue is fixed in version 0.75.0, which removes the Hello handshake and the gob-based token decoding.
  
Severity: 6.3 | MEDIUM

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-124283 - Code execution and SQL injection via struct-wrapped values in a forged keyset pagination cursor in Ash
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-124283
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 2:34 a.m. | 54 minutes ago
  
Description :Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code or inject SQL through a forged keyset pagination cursor.

Ash.Page.Keyset.filter/4 in lib/ash/page/keyset.ex decodes the client-supplied page[:after] or page[:before] cursor from Erlang external term format and rejects decoded expressions with Ash.Expr.expr?/1. That check does not examine the fields of a struct. The cast of each value against the type of its sort field accepts structs for the :ci_string, :map, :struct and :term types. A struct in the cursor value for such a sort field therefore reaches the data layer. With AshPostgres, the read passes such a struct to inspect/1, which runs the Inspect implementation of the struct module that the attacker selected. A chain of struct modules from ecto and db_connection then calls a function that the cursor names, which permits OS command execution. An %Ash.Query.Function.Fragment{} inside an %Ash.CiString{} value is written into the SQL query as raw text.

This issue affects ash: from 3.31.3 before 3.38.0.
  
Severity: 8.9 | HIGH
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-130178 - AutoGPT: The unspecified address :: bypasses the request blocklist and reaches loopback services (SSRF)
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-130178
  
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 1:24 a.m. | 29 minutes ago
  
Description :AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, an incomplete IPv6 blocklist in AutoGPT's outbound SSRF protection allows authenticated users to reach local or private network services. Specifically, _is_ip_blocked and BLOCKED_IP_NETWORKS in autogpt_platform/backend/backend/util/request.py fail to reject the IPv6 unspecified address :: (which connects to ::1 on Linux) as well as 6to4, NAT64, Teredo, and deprecated IPv4-compatible IPv6 encodings. An attacker can pass :: directly to blocks/sql_query_block.py or blocks/email_block.py, or point URL-fetching blocks, web fetch, MCP servers, webhooks, or OAuth at a hostname whose AAAA record resolves to ::. On backends run directly on a host, this exposes unauthenticated internal RPC services and databases listening on ::1, though the default Docker Compose and single-container deployments bind internal services to IPv4 only. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

Description :TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Description :OpenEMR is a free and open source electronic health records and medical practice management application. vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-135617 - Lookyloo Inconsistent Authorization Enforcement for Private Captures Allows Unauthorized Data Access
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-135617
  
Published : Nov. 23, 2026, 8:34 p.m. | 23 minutes ago
  
Description :Lookyloo is a web-based URL capture and analysis platform. Prior to the fix, the authorization mechanism for private captures (seed-based access control) was not consistently enforced at the data access layer. The capture_cache method and numerous internal methods (get_info, get_meta, get_statistics, get_modules_responses, get_data, get_video, get_screenshot, get_har, get_cookies, get_storage_state, get_frames, get_console_messages, get_capture, get_ressource, misp_export, lacus_export, ai_export, comparator functions, and others) could be invoked with only a capture UUID without validating the required seed token. This meant that API endpoints and internal code paths that called these methods directly could return private capture data to unauthenticated users or users lacking the correct seed. The before_request hook in the web interface provided a partial check, but the underlying data layer did not enforce it, creating an inconsistent authorization boundary. An attacker who knew or guessed a private capture UUID could potentially access sensitive data including rendered screenshots, HAR files, downloaded files, cookies, storage state, console messages, and MISP exports through various REST API endpoints and web routes. The fix introduces a LookylooPrivateCapture exception raised at the cache layer when a private capture is accessed without a valid seed, refactors the API to pass CaptureCache objects (already validated) rather than raw UUIDs, and ensures all web and API endpoints propagate the session-known seed or admin status to the data access layer. Background processes use an explicit unsafe=True flag to bypass the check, as they operate server-side with full trust.
  
Severity: 6.9 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-130164 - Hermes Agent: Missing key validation for Bot Desktop screen environment file in non-local terminal backends
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-130164
  
Published : Nov. 23, 2026, 8:18 p.m. | 39 minutes ago
  
Description :Hermes Agent is an open-source autonomous AI agent built by Nous Research for running tool-using workflows across CLI, desktop, and messaging interfaces. From 0.21.6 to 0.23.1, when Bot Desktop is hosted inside a non-local terminal backend, the agent process reads a backend-writable screen environment file without validating keys or values and merges its entries into the environment of processes started on the agent machine. Specifically, when terminal.backend is set to docker or ssh (or a plugin backend declaring supports_streams) with placement auto or terminal, _published() in tools/bot_desktop/sandbox_host.py accepts arbitrary KEY=VALUE lines from the hermes-bot-desktop env file and propagates them via tools/bot_desktop/runtime.py into the browser harness, computer-use helpers, and local terminal children. Code running inside the terminal backend can therefore set variables such as LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, or PATH and gain code execution on the agent machine as the gateway user upon a subsequent browser or computer-use spawn, exposing credentials, tokens, and session history under the Hermes home directory. The default local backend, backends that cannot host a screen (Modal, Daytona, and Vercel), and Hermes Cloud in its default configuration are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.23.2.
  
Severity: 7.8 | HIGH

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-102955 - OpenThread RCP transmits MAC-secured 802.15.4 frames without applying the MAC key when using the PSA crypto backend
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-102955
  
Published : Nov. 23, 2026, 7:17 p.m. | 1 hour, 40 minutes ago
  
Description :The OpenThread PSA crypto platform backend in modules/openthread/platform/crypto_psa.c only supported PSA key references. otPlatCryptoAesSetKey() copied aKey->mKeyRef into the AES context unconditionally. On an OpenThread Radio Co-Processor (RCP) build, CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_CRYPTO_PSA does not select CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_PLATFORM_KEY_REF, so OpenThread passes the MAC key as literal bytes and mKeyRef is uninitialized. psa_cipher_encrypt() in otPlatCryptoAesEncrypt() then fails without writing its output, and the error is only caught by an OpenThread assertion that is compiled to a no-op when CONFIG_ASSERT is disabled.

When the RCP handles transmit security in software, AES-CCM* is never keyed. That is the case with Thread 1.2 or later, where CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_MAC_SOFTWARE_TX_SECURITY_ENABLE defaults to y, on a radio driver without IEEE802154_HW_TX_SEC. Every MAC key-id-mode-1 frame goes out with its payload XORed against a single 16-byte pad of stale stack data, reused for every block, and with an unkeyed MIC. CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_CRYPTO_PSA is enabled by default since v4.4.0.

A passive attacker within 802.15.4 radio range can recover the pad from predictable plaintext (for example 6LoWPAN headers) and read the payload of the frames the device transmits. The practical impact is limited. The configuration is not the default (the default Thread version is 1.1), and the same defect makes peers reject every secured data frame, so an affected device cannot exchange data on the network. Received traffic and key distribution are not affected. With CONFIG_ASSERT enabled, the RCP halts on the first secured transmission instead.
  
Severity: 3.1 | LOW

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-102956 - Ethernet L2 net_pkt reference-count error on ARP request send failure can free an unrelated packet
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-102956
  
Published : Nov. 23, 2026, 7:17 p.m. | 59 minutes ago
  
Description :ethernet_send() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c dropped the caller's reference on an IPv4 packet whenever net_arp_prepare() returned NET_ARP_PKT_REPLACED. That return value is also used when ARP could not queue the packet because every ARP cache entry is already pending. In that case ARP holds no reference of its own, so the original packet was freed before the replacing ARP request was transmitted.

If transmitting the ARP request then failed (a driver send error or an ethernet_fill_header() failure), the error path called net_pkt_ref() on the freed packet. net_if_tx() then called net_pkt_unref() on it again. If the freed net_pkt slab slot was reallocated in between, the stray unref releases a reference owned by an unrelated packet, which is freed while still in use.

An attacker on the local link can drive the ARP cache into the all-pending state. CONFIG_NET_ARP_TABLE_SIZE defaults to 2, so it is enough to elicit replies to a few spoofed, non-responding on-subnet addresses. Reaching the memory corruption also needs a transmit failure the attacker does not directly control and a narrow slab-reuse race. The practical impact is corruption or a crash of the network stack (denial of service).
  
Severity: 3.1 | LOW
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-102954 - Out-of-bounds write from peripheral-supplied block count in STM32 SMBus driver
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-102954
  
Published : Nov. 23, 2026, 7:17 p.m. | 59 minutes ago
  
Description :The STM32 SMBus driver (drivers/smbus/smbus_stm32.c) implements smbus_block_read() and smbus_block_pcall() by issuing a single i2c_transfer() in which the byte-count byte returned by the peripheral is read directly into the len field of the following i2c_msg. That message then receives data straight into the caller-supplied buffer. Nothing bounds the count, so smbus_stm32_block_read() and smbus_stm32_block_pcall() read up to 255 bytes into a buffer that the SMBus API documents (and the syscall verifiers validate) as holding at most SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX (32) bytes.

The count is chosen by the addressed SMBus peripheral. A malicious, counterfeit or faulty device on the bus (for example a removable smart battery, PMBus supply or plug-in module), or anyone able to drive the bus lines, can report a block count above 32 and cause the driver to write up to 223 bytes past the end of the caller's buffer. Callers typically pass a 32-byte stack buffer, as the in-tree smbus block_read shell command does, so the overflow lands on the caller's stack before any caller-side count check can run.

The result is attacker-controlled stack or memory corruption in the context of the calling thread, which can crash the system or potentially be leveraged for code execution. When the call arrives through the smbus_block_read/smbus_block_pcall system calls, the out-of-bounds write happens in supervisor mode beyond the 32-byte region validated for the user thread. The fix receives the block into a driver-local 255-byte buffer and copies it out only when the count is at most SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX, returning -ENODATA otherwise.
  
Severity: 6.8 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-102950 - ZMS mount recovery treats stored value data as allocation table entries, allowing forged entries and storage corruption
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-102950
  
Published : Nov. 23, 2026, 7:17 p.m. | 59 minutes ago
  
Description :The mount-time recovery scan of the Zephyr Memory Storage (ZMS) key-value store, zms_recover_last_ate() in subsys/kvss/zms/zms.c (subsys/fs/zms/zms.c in older releases), computes the end of the sector's data area incorrectly. Every valid allocation table entry (ATE) reset the data-end bound to the start of the sector, including entries whose value is stored inline (8 bytes or less) and delete entries. When the newest ATE in the active sector is one of these, the scan continues past the ATE area into the payload area and reads stored value bytes as struct zms_ate records.

Any payload slot that passes the ATE check (a CRC8 plus the one-byte sector cycle count) is adopted as the newest entry. zms_init() then sets fs->ate_wra and fs->data_wra from it. The pointers are only this weak check away from data an application may have stored on behalf of a remote party: a BLE-writable device name, provisioned credentials, or configuration received over the network. An attacker who can get about 16 bytes of chosen content persisted in a ZMS value can plant a forged ATE. The forged entry takes effect after the next mount, provided the newest entry in that sector is small or a delete. Random data can also match by chance, which is how the issue was found.

A forged or accidentally matched ATE overrides the stored entry for any chosen id. Its inline data or its offset/len pointer controls what later reads of that key return. The misplaced write pointers also make later writes place ATEs and payloads over other entries' existing data, silently corrupting persistent configuration such as settings values stored in ZMS. The effects are limited to the active flash sector and to what ZMS returns to its callers. No RAM out-of-bounds access was identified.
  
Severity: 5.9 | MEDIUM
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-127224 - GFI HelpDesk before 4.99.13 SQL Injection via Archiver ExportAll
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-127224
  
Published : 23 Nov. 2026, 17.26 | 23 menit ago
  
Description :GFI HelpDesk before 4.99.13 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the archiver export feature that allows authenticated attackers with administrator privileges to execute arbitrary SQL queries by supplying crafted itemid[] array values to /admin/index.php?/archiver/Manager/ExportAll. The Controller_Manager.ExportAll() method joins the itemid values with implode() and GetWhere() concatenates them into an IN() clause without sanitization or parameterization, and DumpTables() executes the resulting query against each ticket-related table, allowing attackers to read or modify database contents.

vulnerability.title: CVE-2026-134844 - pgjdbc catalog queries can run objects of other database roles
vulnerability.summary:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-134844
  
Published : Nov. 23, 2026, 4:59 p.m. | 19 minutes ago
  
Description :pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, uses unqualified operators and functions in the catalog queries of DatabaseMetaData, ResultSetMetaData and TypeInfoCache. A role with CREATE on a schema of the application's search_path can add an operator with an exact type match, and the server runs it with the privileges of the application's role. TypeInfoCache also resolves an unqualified type name such as interval by its own ranking. A domain with that name in another schema, even the temporary schema of another session, can be used instead, and its CHECK runs in the application's session. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.
  
Severity: 0.0 | NA
  
  Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...
